metadata.title: The next matching level for triangle-free graphs with bounded degree
metadata.description: For every integer d at least 7, the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free graph with maximum degree at most d and matching number at most d+1 is d squared plus d plus 2. A shortest-odd-cycle deficit argument and five-type equality obstruction prove the fixed-order bound on 2d+3 vertices, and Tutte-Berge extends it to arbitrary order. The attaining construction is due to Banak, Ekim and Taskin; the contribution is the uniform upper bound, resolving the next-matching slice of the Ahanjideh-Ekim-Yildiz conjecture, including the published 184-versus-185 gap at (13,14). A secondary application gives a one-edge bracket for the Bougard-Joret parameters (2d+3,2,d+2), with an unbounded strict-interior discrepancy from the degree-sum prediction. The exact bracket endpoint, remaining AEY matching levels and general revised Bougard-Joret problem remain unresolved. Forty-eight exact graphs, independent matching and connectivity checks, a degree-six boundary control and a rejected complement shortcut accompany the proof. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
